question: Generate a PCA plot using a log2(x+1)-transformed and z-score standardized RNA-seq read count matrix. Color samples by known biological groups. Label the axes with the percentage of variance explained by PC1 and PC2.

files.eval_guideline: Scatter plot must show samples colored by biological group with PC1 and PC2 variance-explained percentages on axes; color palette and marker styles may differ.
files.match_reasoning: The files have the identical basename and PNG image format. The shared task identifier and PCA RNA-seq plot naming establish a clear correspondence.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires semantic plot features—samples colored by biological group and PC1/PC2 axes labeled with variance-explained percentages—while explicitly allowing palette and marker differences. Semantic comparison is therefore appropriate for this PNG output.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images show the same PCA result and scientific message: 30 normal samples form a cluster at negative PC1 and positive PC2, while 60 tumor samples form two clusters at positive PC1, separated along PC2. Both color samples by biological group and label the axes with identical explained-variance values: PC1 at 43.8% and PC2 at 39.3%. The candidate additionally states the log2(x+1) transformation and gene z-scoring in its title, reports group sample sizes in the legend, adds marker outlines, and includes dashed zero-reference lines. These are presentational enhancements and do not change the data or interpretation. Minor differences in figure proportions, typography, point rendering, and axis limits are scientifically immaterial.
